g.text: Imitation learning provides an intuitive policy optimization framework for
executing complex robotic tasks by learning from expert demonstrations
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=1) Imitation learning provides an intuitive policy optimization framework for executing complex robotic tasks by learning from expert demonstrations (Hussein et al., 2017).

However, naively replicating expert behavior can raise safety concerns
during deployment, as the robot's trajectory may become unreliable when
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) However, naively replicating expert behavior can raise safety concerns during deployment, as the robot's trajectory may become unreliable when facing out-of-sample (OOS) states.

g.text: For instance, if the robot begins from an unknown initial state or
encounters environmental perturbations, it could fail to maintain a
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=0) For instance, if the robot begins from an unknown initial state or encounters environmental perturbations, it could fail to maintain a consistent and reliable behavior.

g.text: Model policy as DS with certificates
To address this issue, the policy can be modeled using a dynamical
system (DS) with rigorous reliability certificates (Ravichandar et
g.title: N4 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) To address this issue, the policy can be modeled using a dynamical system (DS) with rigorous reliability certificates (Ravichandar et al., 2020; Dawson et al., 2023).

g.text: One such certificate is asymptotic stability (Devaney, 2021),
which ensures that all trajectories eventually converge to the
same equilibrium state, regardless of the initial condition or
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=4) One such certificate is asymptotic stability (Devaney, 2021), which ensures that all trajectories eventually converge to the same equilibrium state, regardless of the initial condition or perturbations (Khansari-Zadeh & Billard, 2011; Rana et al., 2020; Abyaneh et al., 2024).

g.text: While asymptotic stability guarantees convergence, it overlooks
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=1) While asymptotic stability guarantees convergence, it overlooks the transient behavior (Tsukamoto et al., 2021).

g.text: Contractive DS: trajectories converge to each other
In contrast, contractive DS policies ensure that the resulting
trajectories exponentially converge to each other, and ultimately
to the equilibrium state (Ravichandar et al., 2017; Mohammadi et
g.title: N8 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) In contrast, contractive DS policies ensure that the resulting trajectories exponentially converge to each other, and ultimately to the equilibrium state (Ravichandar et al., 2017; Mohammadi et al., 2024).

g.text: We leverage the stronger notion of contractivity (Lohmiller &
Slotine, 1998) to ensure reliability in the transient phase, and
as a result, enhance the imitation quality.
g.title: N9 [Method] (cites=1) We leverage the stronger notion of contractivity (Lohmiller & Slotine, 1998) to ensure reliability in the transient phase, and as a result, enhance the imitation quality.

g.text: Two approaches to contractive DS learning
There are two main approaches to learning contractive DSs.
g.title: N10 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) There are two main approaches to learning contractive DSs.

g.text: The most common method relies on constrained optimization to train
the DS while satisfying learned or fixed contractivity
certificates (Ravichandar et al., 2017; Blocher et al., 2017;
g.title: N10a [Prior_Work] (cites=3) The most common method relies on constrained optimization to train the DS while satisfying learned or fixed contractivity certificates (Ravichandar et al., 2017; Blocher et al., 2017; Sindhwani et al., 2018).

g.text: However, constrained optimization is computationally challenging
for complex expert behaviors or high-dimensional state spaces.
g.title: N11a [Limitation] (cites=0) However, constrained optimization is computationally challenging for complex expert behaviors or high-dimensional state spaces.

g.text: Additionally, most constrained approaches trade off imitation
g.title: N11b [Limitation] (cites=0) Additionally, most constrained approaches trade off imitation accuracy for constraint satisfaction.

g.text: The second approach is based on parameterized models with built-in
contractivity guarantees for any choice of parameters (Mohammadi
g.title: N10b [Prior_Work] (cites=2) The second approach is based on parameterized models with built-in contractivity guarantees for any choice of parameters (Mohammadi et al., 2024; Dawson et al., 2023).

g.text: Model stays contractive under imperfect training
As a result, the model remains contractive even if the learning process is
g.title: N12 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) As a result, the model remains contractive even if the learning process is imperfect or disrupted.

g.text: In this work, we build on the foundation of two such formulations:
(i) a parameterization of contractive continuous-time DSs using
g.title: N13 [Method] (cites=2) In this work, we build on the foundation of two such formulations: (i) a parameterization of contractive continuous-time DSs using recurrent equilibrium networks (RENs) (Martinelli et al., 2023), and (ii) the coupling layer architecture (Papamakarios et al., 2021).

g.text: RENs: adjustable rate; coupling: contraction-preserving bijection
The former ensures that the DS is contractive with an adjustable rate, while
the latter provides a trainable bijective transformation that preserves
g.title: N14 [Method] (cites=0) The former ensures that the DS is contractive with an adjustable rate, while the latter provides a trainable bijective transformation that preserves contraction properties.

g.text: Our experiments demonstrate that the coupling layers enhance the model's
representation power, leading to improved imitation accuracy and faster
training, while maintaining the contractive nature of the DS.
g.title: N15 [Result] (cites=0) Our experiments demonstrate that the coupling layers enhance the model's representation power, leading to improved imitation accuracy and faster training, while maintaining the contractive nature of the DS.

g.text: Contributions. We propose a State-only framework for learning Contractive
Dynamical System policies (SCDS), which offers several distinct advantages.
g.title: N16 [Contribution] (cites=0) Contributions. We propose a State-only framework for learning Contractive Dynamical System policies (SCDS), which offers several distinct advantages.

g.text: First, SCDS learns the policy solely from
state measurements, eliminating the need to
g.title: N16a [Contribution] (cites=0) First, SCDS learns the policy solely from state measurements, eliminating the need to measure the expert's velocity.

g.text: Hence, we address the cumulative error problem observed in
previous methods that replicate expert velocity, where small
errors can accumulate and lead to significant deviations in state
g.title: N16b [Contribution] (cites=2) Hence, we address the cumulative error problem observed in previous methods that replicate expert velocity, where small errors can accumulate and lead to significant deviations in state space trajectories (Ravichandar et al., 2020; Abyaneh et al., 2024).

g.text: Additionally, SCDS enables learning in a
latent space, with its dimension adapting
g.title: N16c [Contribution] (cites=0) Additionally, SCDS enables learning in a latent space, with its dimension adapting to the problem at hand.

g.text: It facilitates learning in high-dimensional state spaces by
mapping to lower-dimensional latent representations, while also
providing flexibility in low-dimensional spaces through
g.title: N16d [Contribution] (cites=0) It facilitates learning in high-dimensional state spaces by mapping to lower-dimensional latent representations, while also providing flexibility in low-dimensional spaces through higher-dimensional embeddings.

g.text: From a theoretical standpoint, we provide a
rigorous solution for OOS recovery by
establishing an upper bound on the
g.title: N16e [Contribution] (cites=0) From a theoretical standpoint, we provide a rigorous solution for OOS recovery by establishing an upper bound on the worst-case deviation from expert trajectories.

g.text: SCDS also offers control over the transient
g.title: N16f [Contribution] (cites=0) SCDS also offers control over the transient behavior through an adjustable and learnable contraction rate.

g.text: Training SCDS is highly efficient by
g.title: N16g [Contribution] (cites=1) Training SCDS is highly efficient by relying on unconstrained optimization and neural ordinary differential equations (ODE) fixed-point differentiation for gradient computation (Chen et al., 2018).
